understanding: Three new chapters for OKO, NOT a rebuild of the done 5-stage foundation. (1) Empty/background-scene sampling: extend CropCollector to periodically (timer or N frames without detection, ~5-10 min) store negative frames (no person/animal AND scene-memory says background-only) labelled class='background'/'empty' into runs/labels/<cam>/, so the fine-tuned model learns 'empty=empty' and stops hallucinating. (2) A nightly (~01:00-06:00) self-correcting retrain loop: day's collection (positives + empties + hard-negatives) -> gemini-2.5-flash labelling (training-time only) -> DatasetExporter (YOLO) -> FinetuneGate (eval held-out, train on GPU, promote ONLY if better on person-precision AND accuracy, else rollback), with idempotent catch-up of missed nights and live-inference pause/timebox while the GPU trains. (3) First real run is a DRY-RUN: train+compare+Telegram verdict with before/after metrics, NO auto-promote until the operator confirms; and a mandatory verify-by-code that the FinetuneGate fix (99034ac5) is genuinely correct. I read the live code: the gate fix is in fact NOT correct (gates on accuracy only, reads classification .probs instead of detection .boxes, compares class-ids vs class_name so nothing ever matches, non-atomic promote), which makes the verify-by-code chapter the true critical path.
summary: Sequence the work gate-first, поглавно, atom = 1 file + 1 test, each gated by `pytest oko` and reviewed by Architect-Claude. Chapter 0 is a verify-by-code pass whose FAILING assertions become the spec to re-fix FinetuneGate (detection outputs via .boxes, class-id->name mapping, person-precision AND accuracy, atomic os.replace promote). Only then build the negatives path (CropCollector.collect_background + a debounced timer in LivePipeline.run, using empty-label YOLO negatives rather than 'background' boxes), a dataset balancer (positives:empty:hard-neg ratio with a logged manifest), and a single idempotent CLI entrypoint `python -m oko.training.nightly_run --date YYYY-MM-DD [--dry-run]` that the OS scheduler (Windows Task Scheduler) or the existing bridge nightly mechanism merely triggers. Idempotency/catch-up via per-date marker dirs with terminal STATUS files; GPU contention via a TRAINING.lock the live service honours plus a night-window timebox watchdog. Ship with config training.auto_promote=FALSE so the first (and every) run is a dry-run posting before/after person-precision & accuracy to Telegram until the operator flips the flag.

decision_atoms.statement: Treat FinetuneGate fix 99034ac5 as NOT verified and ship with auto-promotion DISABLED; Chapter 0 is a verify-by-code pass whose failing assertions are the re-fix spec.
decision_atoms.reason: Reading src/oko/training/finetune_gate.py at HEAD: compare_on_held_out gates on accuracy ONLY (line 50, no person-precision); _predict_all reads results[0].probs.top1 — a classification head that is None for a YOLO detection model, so every prediction becomes '__missing__'; predictions are stringified class-ids ('0') while EvalHarness compares against class_name ('person'), so actual==predicted can never hold; promote_or_rollback unlink()+copy2 is non-atomic. So 'done' is false and trusting it would let a worse or randomly-scored model promote — exactly the literary-slop failure the task warns about.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Pushes the headline nightly-retrain feature behind one corrective chapter and makes the gate the critical path, but it is the only way to honour the person-precision-AND-accuracy and atomic-promote constraints.

decision_atoms.statement: Re-fix the gate as its own atom: _predict_all consumes detection outputs (results[0].boxes, top-confidence box's cls) mapped through the dataset names[] to label STRINGS; promote iff new.per_class['person'].precision >= current AND new.accuracy >= current, each with a configurable epsilon margin.
decision_atoms.reason: EvalHarness already computes per_class[label]['precision'] keyed by class_name and an overall accuracy, so the metrics the person-precision-AND-accuracy gate needs already exist — only FinetuneGate's prediction extraction and comparison are wrong. Using .boxes + names[] makes predicted/actual comparable and makes 'person-precision' a real number.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Reducing detection output to one top-box label per crop is a simplification of full mAP/IoU eval; adequate for a per-crop promotion gate but not a COCO-style detection evaluation.

decision_atoms.statement: Make promotion crash-safe: copy candidate best.pt to a temp path beside the current-weights link, archive the old weights first, then os.replace() (atomic rename on the same NTFS volume).
decision_atoms.reason: The current unlink()+copy2 leaves a window with no current weights; a crash mid-promote bricks live inference. os.replace is atomic within one volume.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires the temp file on the same drive as the weights link; negligible cost.

decision_atoms.statement: Add CropCollector.collect_background(camera_id, frame_rgb, frame_id, timestamp, reason) and trigger it from LivePipeline.run() on a debounced timer (every 5-10 min) ONLY when the frame has no person/animal detection AND scene memory reports background-only.
decision_atoms.reason: Today CropCollector.collect() requires a Detection and is invoked only on VLM-confirmed positives (live.py:454), so no negatives are ever stored. A separate background path keyed on no-detection + scene-memory gives clean negatives without bbox guesswork.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds small state (last-empty-capture time, no-detection counter) to the ~30fps hot loop; must stay cheap so it does not disturb capture cadence.

decision_atoms.statement: Represent empties as YOLO-canonical background IMAGES with EMPTY label files (true negatives), not as 'background' object boxes — keep nc/names back-compatible but stop emitting a class-2 box for negatives.
decision_atoms.reason: DatasetExporter currently writes a class-2 bbox line for every background crop (dataset_exporter.py:54,61), i.e. it teaches 'background' as a detectable object, which does not directly suppress person/animal false positives. Ultralytics learns 'empty=empty' from images that have no label lines.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Switching to empty-label negatives changes the dataset contract and some existing exporter tests; treating background as a class is simpler but pedagogically wrong for FP suppression. Worth an A/B on held-out FP rate before fully committing.

decision_atoms.statement: Add an explicit balancer in the nightly export: cap and ratio positives : empty-negatives : hard-negatives (~3:1:1, configurable) with deterministic seeded sampling and a logged manifest of counts kept/dropped.
decision_atoms.reason: Unbounded negatives will swamp the few daily positives and collapse recall; the task explicitly demands balancing, and 'no silent caps' means logging what was sampled out.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Hard-negatives (operator-rejected false alarms) need a concrete source/label; if that feed does not yet exist it becomes its own small prerequisite chapter rather than a free input.

decision_atoms.statement: Implement the night job as a single idempotent CLI entrypoint `python -m oko.training.nightly_run --date YYYY-MM-DD [--dry-run]` that wires collect->label->export->eval->gate->(promote|rollback); the scheduler only invokes it.
decision_atoms.reason: Separating 'what runs' from 'when it runs' makes the whole pipeline unit-testable under pytest oko (one fixture-driven end-to-end test) and lets either Windows Task Scheduler or the existing bridge nightly mechanism drive it. An injected clock + --date keeps non-deterministic time out of the testable core.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Two moving parts (entrypoint + OS trigger) instead of one, but coupling the logic directly to Task Scheduler would make it effectively untestable.

decision_atoms.statement: Idempotency and catch-up via per-date marker dirs runs/training/<date>/ with a terminal STATUS file (PENDING->TRAINED->PROMOTED/ROLLED_BACK/DRYRUN); on start, no-op if today is terminal, else process the most recent date lacking a terminal status.
decision_atoms.reason: A missed night (machine off) must be caught up exactly once and a re-run of a complete night must be a no-op; file-marker state survives restarts and is trivial to unit-test.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Default catch-up processes only the latest missed night to bound GPU time; deeper historical backfill is opt-in rather than automatic.

decision_atoms.statement: Guard the single GPU with a lockfile runs/training/TRAINING.lock written before train() and removed in a finally block; the live service watches it and pauses inference, and train() runs under a timebox watchdog that aborts+rolls back if it exceeds the night window.
decision_atoms.reason: One GPU cannot run live inference and YOLO training simultaneously; an explicit lock plus timebox prevents both OOM and a runaway train bleeding into daytime. The task explicitly mandates pause/timebox of live inference during training.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Pausing live inference opens a night-time blind spot; acceptable per the task but it must be bounded to 01:00-06:00 and logged, ideally with a lightweight motion-only fallback.

decision_atoms.statement: Default config training.auto_promote=FALSE: every run until the operator flips it executes train+compare and Telegrams before/after person-precision & accuracy plus the gate verdict, but calls promote ONLY if auto_promote AND gate passed; otherwise archive the candidate and roll back.
decision_atoms.reason: Directly satisfies the dry-run-first constraint and keeps a human in the loop until the freshly re-fixed gate has been observed to behave in production.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: No model can ever promote without a manual flag flip until the operator opts in — which is the intended safety property, not a defect.

assumptions: The finetune_gate.py I read at HEAD is the post-99034ac5 state (the 'done' fix); if a newer un-merged fix exists elsewhere, atoms 1-3 must be re-validated against it first.
The training machine has a single GPU shared between live inference and YOLO training.
A hard-negative source (operator-rejected alerts / false alarms, e.g. from Telegram feedback) exists or can be derived; if not, building it is a prerequisite chapter, not a free input.
The existing 3-class taxonomy person/animal/background is the intended detector scheme.
gemini-2.5-flash labelling runs only inside the night job; the live path never calls Gemini for labels.
`pytest oko` is the authoritative gate and currently passes on master.
A Telegram notifier hook exists (FinetuneGate already accepts telegram_notifier) and can be wired to the operator chat for before/after verdicts.

risks.risk: Re-fixed gate is still subtly wrong and promotes a worse model ('green' but lying).
risks.mitigation: auto_promote defaults FALSE + a dedicated regression test that feeds a deliberately-worse candidate and asserts NO promotion + adversarial Architect-Claude review of the gate atom specifically.

risks.risk: Negative oversampling collapses recall (model learns to predict nothing).
risks.mitigation: Ratio cap (atom 6) + track held-out person-recall as a secondary guard so a recall drop also blocks promotion.

risks.risk: Background-as-class mislabelling fails to reduce false positives and adds a spurious detectable class.
risks.mitigation: Adopt empty-label negatives (atom 5) and A/B the two representations on held-out FP rate before committing the dataset contract.

risks.risk: Paused live inference creates a nightly security blind spot.
risks.mitigation: Timebox training strictly to the 01:00-06:00 window, log start/stop, and run a lightweight motion-only fallback during training.

risks.risk: Train crash / OOM mid-promote leaves no usable current weights.
risks.mitigation: Atomic os.replace promote (atom 3) + archived rollback target + lockfile cleanup and weights integrity check in a finally block.

risks.risk: Idempotency race or double-run from two schedulers firing.
risks.mitigation: Exclusive lock on the per-date marker dir; a second concurrent invocation no-ops; terminal STATUS prevents reprocessing.

risks.risk: Scheduler never fires (Task Scheduler disabled or machine asleep), silently skipping training.
risks.mitigation: Catch-up scan on next boot + a Telegram heartbeat alert when no training ran the previous night.

risks.risk: Gemini labelling cost or quality drift corrupts the training set.
risks.mitigation: Cache labels per crop, periodic sample-audit of Gemini labels, keep labelling strictly training-time-only.

minimal_version: A safe, mostly-manual slice that delivers the negatives plus a trustworthy gate without yet automating promotion: (1) CropCollector.collect_background + a debounced timer in LivePipeline.run using empty-label YOLO negatives; (2) verify-by-code tests that FAIL against the current gate (proving the 99034ac5 claims); (3) re-fix FinetuneGate — detection outputs via .boxes, class-id->name mapping, person-precision AND accuracy, atomic os.replace promote — until those tests pass; (4) a hand-run `python -m oko.training.nightly_run --dry-run --date <today>` that collects->labels->exports->evals->prints and Telegrams the before/after verdict with training.auto_promote=FALSE. No OS scheduler, no catch-up, no live-pause yet. Each step is one file + one test, gated by `pytest oko` and reviewed by Architect-Claude.
advanced_version: Full autonomy on top of the minimal slice: Windows Task Scheduler (or the existing bridge nightly mechanism) triggers the idempotent entrypoint nightly at ~01:00; per-date marker dirs give exactly-once execution plus catch-up of the last missed night; balanced positives:empty:hard-negative datasets with logged manifests; a TRAINING.lock pauses live inference under a night-window timebox watchdog with a motion-only fallback; after the operator flips training.auto_promote=true the re-fixed gate auto-promotes on person-precision AND accuracy improvement and atomically rolls back otherwise, every run posting before/after metrics to Telegram; a periodic background A/B of 'background-as-class' vs empty-label negatives on held-out FP rate; and archive retention with a one-command rollback to any of the last N weights.
